subject: Bound hosted producer context memory and route session verification to its focused owner
claim: Producer contexts retain 3560 bytes of fingerprints instead of 24408113 bytes on Windows and 24404721 bytes on Debian. All 72 inventory artifacts remain read and digest-checked. Context preparation changed from 120 to 73 ms on Windows and from 2733 to 850 ms on Debian; thirty repeated key-hash passes changed from 374/394 to 6/9 ms. Cached two-profile packaging passed with identical bytes and behavior in 23390 ms on Windows and 23962 ms on Debian. Session changes select the existing cache owner instead of a 2540-second database plan, and its twelve cases passed on both hosts.

limitations: Single observations with retained tool artifacts. These are not controlled clean-host benchmarks or stable wall-clock thresholds. The workload uses an 82115-byte enum-request WVB, not the full compiler toolset or full qualification graph.

Retained producer bytes count Buffer payloads held by the context, excluding JavaScript object overhead. RSS/external-memory values in diagnostic outputs are process snapshots after explicit garbage collection, not peak memory or aggregate child-process memory. The main PowerShell peak is recorded separately.

The previous paired cached workload took 23684 ms on Windows and 31628 ms on Debian, as recorded in the related image-reuse evidence. The Windows timing difference is small; the clearer Windows benefits are lower retained bytes and repeated hashing cost.

Bounded concurrent preparation preserves input coverage and deterministic order. It retains only eight-byte little-endian sizes and SHA-256 digests; the existing focused session test enforces a 4096-byte producer payload bound and checks every fingerprint against source bytes. Hosted keys use format 2 and include the implementation plus Node version; segmented image keys also include Node version.

The implementation changed-file gate completed before documentation extraction. The original shared checkpoint specification still conservatively selects database verification when it changes; its hosted section was relocated into a new focused specification. The unchanged database behavior contracts were not rerun for this documentation relocation.

Complete database, compiler, bootstrap, and paired-host qualification were not run because they are unrelated to these cache contracts and exceed the local development budget. Overall verification redesign and qualification targets remain incomplete.
